sits_in: Bank event log (LOS/LMS/app/txn/collection)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Stamped automatically by whichever system recorded the event.
what_it_means: 'Event timestamp' — the exact date and time a thing happened (an application submitted, a login, a payment). 'ts' is just short for 'timestamp'.
why_it_matters: Location clues go stale. A login from Pune last week is far stronger evidence than one from 2022. Time is how the tool knows which clues to trust most.
derived_columns: signal_age_days = how many days ago this happened (newer = stronger).  event_hour = hour of day 0-23.  event_dayofweek = Mon-Sun.  latest_signal_flag = is this the case's most recent signal? (yes/no).

sits_in: Bank/application/collections logs  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Recorded by the system that logged the event.
what_it_means: A label for WHAT happened: application_submit, login, repayment, field_visit, returned_mail, etc.
why_it_matters: Different events carry different trust. A field visit that physically confirmed someone is worth far more than a casual login. The type tells the tool how much weight to give the clue.
derived_columns: event_trust_weight = a number for how much to trust this kind of event (a field visit > a login).  signal_source_type = a tidy category of where the clue came from.

sits_in: Bank system metadata  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Tagged by the bank's data pipeline.
what_it_means: Which internal system produced this row (the mobile app, the LOS, the CRM, etc.).
why_it_matters: Helps trace data quality and ownership — some systems are cleaner than others, and knowing the origin helps debugging and auditing.
derived_columns: source_priority = which system to believe first if two disagree.  audit_source = a clean label kept for tracing/debugging.

sits_in: App/web/server login logs  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Captured automatically by the bank's app or website server the moment the customer connects.
what_it_means: The public internet address the customer's device used (e.g. 103.21.244.1) — think of it as the 'return address' of their internet connection at that moment.
why_it_matters: It is the main location clue you can enrich with free public APIs — it gives an approximate city and flags like VPN/proxy. It is NOT the home address, but it's a real, cheap signal.
derived_columns: ip_country / ip_state / ip_city = the place the IP resolves to.  ip_lat / ip_lon = its map point.  isp = the internet provider.  asn = the network number.  proxy_flag / hosting_flag = true if it's a VPN/proxy/datacentre (then trust the location less).

sits_in: Application / KYC record (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Part of the address the customer wrote on the form; held in the bank's record.
what_it_means: The 6-digit PIN-code of the declared address. A PIN is a small postal area, so it pins location to roughly a neighbourhood, not a whole state.
why_it_matters: It is the cheapest, fastest consistency check: a PIN maps to exactly one real district/state, so if the declared city/state doesn't match the PIN's real one, that's an instant red flag.
derived_columns: pincode_state / pincode_district = the real state/district that PIN belongs to.  pincode_zone = the broad postal zone (first digit of the PIN).  pincode_valid_flag = does this PIN actually exist? (yes/no).

sits_in: Application record (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Text the customer typed on the form.
what_it_means: The city name the customer declared (free text, so spellings vary: 'Bengaluru' / 'Bangalore').
why_it_matters: Lets you cross-check the city against the PIN's real district/state and catch contradictions. Useful only after cleaning the spelling. Data preprocessing
derived_columns: declared_city_lat_lon = the city turned into map coordinates.  city_state_match_flag = does the declared city actually sit in the declared/PIN state? (catches contradictions).

sits_in: Application record (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Text the customer typed on the form.
what_it_means: The state the customer declared.
why_it_matters: A broad regional cross-check against the PIN and city. Needs spelling/old-name normalisation (e.g. old vs new state names) to be reliable. Data preprocessing
derived_columns: declared_macro_region = the broad region (North/South/etc.) of the state.  state_normalized = the cleaned, standard spelling of the state name.

sits_in: Application / KYC record (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: The complete address line the customer wrote.
what_it_means: The full street address (house, street, area, city, state).
why_it_matters: Useful for precise geocoding and address matching, but sends personal data to geocoders?
derived_columns: address_geocode_confidence = if ever geocoded, how confident the match is (0-1).  (Parked for now — not used in this sheet.)

sits_in: Loan account record (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: From the loan record — the branch that sourced/disbursed the loan.
what_it_means: The 11-character branch code (e.g. HDFC0000037). The first 4 letters are the bank; the rest identify the branch. It maps to one specific branch city.
why_it_matters: The branch a loan came from is a real-world clue to where the customer operates/transacts — an operational anchor, not proof of where they live.
derived_columns: branch_city / branch_district / branch_state = where the branch physically is.  branch_region = its broad region.

sits_in: LOS / branch master (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: From the loan-origination record when an IFSC isn't captured.
what_it_means: An internal branch code used to identify which branch sourced the loan.
why_it_matters: Joins to the bank's branch master to recover the branch geography even without an IFSC.
derived_columns: sourcing_branch_city / sourcing_branch_state = the city/state of the branch that sourced the loan.

sits_in: Loan servicing system (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: From the loan-servicing record.
what_it_means: The branch currently servicing the account (may differ from where it was sourced).
why_it_matters: Hints where the relationship/recovery team sits — useful context, though it reflects bank operations more than the borrower's movement.
derived_columns: servicing_branch_state = the state of the branch currently servicing the account.

sits_in: App telemetry / fraud-stack logs (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Generated by the bank's app/website from device characteristics, then hashed.
what_it_means: A scrambled fingerprint of the customer's phone/computer (a code, not the real device). The SAME device produces the SAME hash.
why_it_matters: It reveals if one device is behind many 'different' applicants — the classic shape of a fraud ring.
derived_columns: device_seen_states = the states this device has appeared in.  same_device_many_customers = true if many 'different' people share this one device (ring tell).  device_case_count = how many cases this device touches.

sits_in: Mobile app telemetry (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Issued by the app when it is installed.
what_it_means: An identifier for ONE installation of the bank app on one device.
why_it_matters: Helps detect the same app install repeating actions across many cases.
derived_columns: app_instance_event_count = how many events came from this one app installation.

sits_in: App/web session logs (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Created per browsing/app session and hashed.
what_it_means: A code for one continuous session of use (one sitting).
why_it_matters: Groups the IP, device, and user-agent seen together in one session so they can be cross-checked.
derived_columns: session_signal_count = how many clues were captured in this one session.  session_region_consistency = do the IP/device/etc. in this session all point to the same region? (yes/no).

sits_in: Browser/app logs (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Sent automatically by the browser/app with every request; recorded in logs.
what_it_means: A short text string the browser/app announces about itself — e.g. 'Mozilla/5.0 ... Android 13 ... Chrome'. It self-describes the device/OS/browser.
why_it_matters: Lets you read the OS/browser/device type and spot odd automation (bots, emulators). It is NOT a location signal on its own.
derived_columns: os_type = Android/iOS/Windows.  browser_family = Chrome/Safari/etc.  device_type = phone/desktop/emulator.

sits_in: Browser/app/device settings (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Read from the device settings.
what_it_means: The timezone the device is set to (e.g. Asia/Kolkata).
why_it_matters: A weak consistency check — if the IP says one country but the timezone says another, something's off. It can be changed manually, so it's only supporting evidence.
derived_columns: timezone_ip_match_flag = does the device's timezone agree with the IP's country/region? (a mismatch is suspicious).

sits_in: Browser/app/device settings (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Read from the device/app settings.
what_it_means: The language/locale set on the device (e.g. te-IN = Telugu-India, kn-IN = Kannada-India).
why_it_matters: A very weak cultural/regional hint — never proof. Kind of supporting evidence only.
derived_columns: locale_region_hint = a very weak regional hint from the language (e.g. kn-IN hints Karnataka). Soft support only — never decide on this alone.

sits_in: Bank app location store (consented)  — needs customer consent + permission
where_it_comes_from: Read by the bank app from the device GPS, only if the user granted location permission(permissions asked typcially during the login)
what_it_means: The latitude (north-south coordinate) of the device at the time of use.
why_it_matters: With consent and a good accuracy figure, GPS is the single most precise location signal that exists.
derived_columns: gps_state / gps_district = the state/district the GPS point falls in.  gps_distance_to_declared_pin = how far the GPS is from the declared address, in km (a big gap is suspicious).

sits_in: Bank app location store (consented)  — needs customer consent + permission
where_it_comes_from: Read by the bank app from device GPS, only with permission.
what_it_means: The longitude (east-west coordinate); pairs with latitude to make a map point.
why_it_matters: Together with gps_lat it gives an exact map location — strongest signal when lawfully consented.
derived_columns: pairs with gps_lat to make the map point; together they feed gps_state / gps_district.

sits_in: Device geolocation API (consented)  — needs customer consent + permission
where_it_comes_from: Returned by the device alongside the GPS fix.
what_it_means: The uncertainty radius of the GPS reading, in metres (e.g. 30 = accurate to ~30 m; 2000 = very rough). This is an issue was looking into.....
why_it_matters: A coordinate without its accuracy is dangerous — 30 m means a building, 2000 m means a whole locality. This tells you how much to trust the point.
derived_columns: gps_accuracy_bucket = grouped accuracy (<50 m good / 50-500 m ok / >500 m rough).  gps_trust_level = how much to trust this particular fix.

sits_in: Device-side Wi-Fi scan (consented)  — needs customer consent + permission
where_it_comes_from: Observed by the device when it scans nearby Wi-Fi, then hashed.
what_it_means: Hashed identifiers of Wi-Fi access points the device can 'see' around it.
why_it_matters: Can place a device even when GPS is weak — but only from consented, device-side observations.
derived_columns: wifi_position_lat_lon = the position estimated from nearby Wi-Fi.  wifi_accuracy = its uncertainty in metres.

sits_in: Device-side cellular observation (consented)  — needs customer consent + permission
where_it_comes_from: Observed by the device from the cell network it's on.
what_it_means: The cell-tower/network identifiers the device sees (MCC=country code, e.g. 404=India; MNC=operator; LAC/CellID=the tower area).
why_it_matters: Supports coarse-to-medium location via a positioning API — but the DEVICE must report it; a phone number alone can never give this.
derived_columns: cell_position_lat_lon = the position estimated from the cell tower.  cell_accuracy = its uncertainty in metres.

sits_in: Bank app/web login logs  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: The bank's own record of every past login.
what_it_means: A history of logins with their time, IP, device, and channel.
why_it_matters: Repeated geography is far stronger than one signal — where someone logs in from again and again is a real location anchor.
derived_columns: most_frequent_login_state_90d = the state they log in from most over 90 days.  last_login_state = the state of their latest login.

sits_in: Payment / loan systems (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: The bank's record of repayment attempts.
what_it_means: A history of repayment attempts and the channels used over time.
why_it_matters: Behaviour AFTER default (when, how, from where they pay) is often fresher and more useful than the old application data.
derived_columns: last_repayment_state = where the latest repayment came from.  repayment_channel_region = the region implied by how/where they pay.

sits_in: CRM / call-centre (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Logged by the bank's CRM/contact centre.
what_it_means: Records of customer support/contact attempts (calls, chats).
why_it_matters: Can surface updated numbers, regions, and whether the person is reachable — useful for recovery prioritisation.
derived_columns: last_contact_success_state = the state where they were last reached.  contactability_flag = are they currently reachable? (yes/no).

sits_in: Dormant-account / card system (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Raised by the bank when a long-inactive card/account suddenly becomes active again.
what_it_means: A flag (plus its date and the channel/IP that woke it) showing a sleeping account came back to life.
why_it_matters: Sleeper accounts waking up is a classic fraud tell, and the reactivation usually carries a fresh IP/device/location — a live, current clue.
lookup_api: No external API (bank's own account-status system).
derived_columns: reactivation_flag = did a long-dormant account suddenly go active? (yes/no).  reactivation_ip_state = the state of the IP used to wake it.  days_dormant_before = how long it slept before reactivating.

sits_in: Core banking / card switch (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: From the bank's transaction systems.
what_it_means: The city/state where an ATM cash event happened on the customer's card/account.
why_it_matters: A physical ATM withdrawal ties the person to a real place at a real time — strong evidence of recent presence.
derived_columns: last_atm_state = state of the most recent ATM use.  frequent_atm_state = the state they use ATMs in most.

sits_in: Card / POS transaction data (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: From card/POS transaction records.
what_it_means: The merchant city/state for card swipes (Point Of Sale = shop card machine).
why_it_matters: Shows where the person actually spends — though the merchant's registered city can differ from where the swipe physically happened.
derived_columns: last_pos_state = state of the latest card swipe.  frequent_pos_city = the city they swipe in most.

sits_in: UPI / payment rails / bank logs  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: From UPI/payment logs.
what_it_means: Metadata about UPI payees/merchants/VPAs (a VPA is a UPI handle like name@bank) and channels.
why_it_matters: Can give merchant or payer geography clues and show where money is moving now — but a UPI handle's suffix alone usually reveals little location.
derived_columns: upi_merchant_region_hint = any region hint from the merchant/payee details (usually weak).

sits_in: Branch / core banking (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: From branch transaction records.
what_it_means: The branch where cash/cheque was deposited or a repayment was made in person.
why_it_matters: A physical branch touchpoint is a clean operational clue — though it could be a third party paying on the customer's behalf.
derived_columns: cash_deposit_state = the state of the branch where cash/cheque was deposited.

sits_in: Collections / field-ops system (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Recorded by a recovery agent who visited an address.
what_it_means: The PIN where a field agent attempted a visit.
why_it_matters: A human physically going to a location is among the most valuable signals for recovery — especially paired with the outcome.
derived_columns: last_visit_pin = the PIN of the most recent field visit.  visit_region = its broad region.

sits_in: Collections / field-ops (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: Logged by the agent after the visit.
what_it_means: The standardised result of the visit: met / shifted / door_locked / wrong_address / neighbour_confirmed, etc.
why_it_matters: It tells you whether a location is CONFIRMED or REJECTED — the outcome matters more than the visit location alone.
derived_columns: presence_confirmed_flag = did the visit confirm the person is there? (yes/no).  address_failed_flag = did it confirm the address is wrong / they moved? (yes/no).

sits_in: Courier / notice dispatch system (bank)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: From the notice/letter dispatch and return records.
what_it_means: The PIN a posted notice was sent to (and returned from, if undelivered).
why_it_matters: Shows whether a declared/served address physically worked or failed — a practical validity check.
derived_columns: mail_return_region = region a returned notice came back from.  notice_delivery_flag = was the notice delivered or returned?

sits_in: Courier / notice vendor (bank/partner)  — bank-internal; needs bank permission
where_it_comes_from: From the courier's tracking feed.
what_it_means: The delivery result: delivered / undelivered / refused / shifted, etc.
why_it_matters: A practical signal of whether the address is real and reachable; vendor data quality varies.
derived_columns: delivery_success_flag = delivered? (yes/no).  delivery_failure_reason = why it failed (moved / refused / wrong address).

sits_in: Credit-bureau report (personal-info section)  — external regulated access; lender pull with consent/permission
where_it_comes_from: Returned by a credit bureau when the lender pulls the report on its own applicant.
what_it_means: The list of CURRENT and PREVIOUS addresses (plus phones/employment) the bureaus hold for that PAN.
why_it_matters: One of the strongest historical-address sources there is — previous addresses are often exactly where an absconder resurfaces.
derived_columns: bureau_last_state = the most recent address state on the bureau file.  bureau_state_count = how many distinct address states they've had.  address_stability_score = 0-1 settledness score.

sits_in: CKYC Registry (CERSAI)  — external regulated access; lender pull with consent/permission
where_it_comes_from: The key used to retrieve a record from the central KYC registry.
what_it_means: An identifier that fetches a person's CKYC record (the once-collected, reusable KYC held centrally by CERSAI).
why_it_matters: Gives an independent, official KYC address history to cross-check the declared address.
derived_columns: ckyc_state = the state on the central-KYC address.  ckyc_last_updated_days = how old that KYC record is, in days.

sits_in: Account Aggregator (AA/FIU flow)  — needs customer consent + permission
where_it_comes_from: Created when the customer approves a consent request in the AA system.
what_it_means: A digital 'yes' that lets the lender securely fetch the customer's bank-statement data through the RBI Account-Aggregator framework.
why_it_matters: It is the clean, consented key to financial behaviour — where money moves now, salary employer, etc.
derived_columns: aa_transaction_geo_hints_available_flag = whether the consented statements actually contain any usable location hints (yes/no).

sits_in: Account Aggregator bank-statement data  — needs customer consent + permission
where_it_comes_from: Parsed from the bank-statement transactions returned via AA.
what_it_means: The free-text descriptions on each transaction (e.g. salary-credit text, merchant names).
why_it_matters: These sometimes contain employer/merchant/city clues — a fresh, consented location hint, though the text is messy.
derived_columns: employer_hint = an employer name guessed from salary-credit text.  merchant_city_hint = a city guessed from merchant text.

sits_in: Platform API (consented)  — needs customer consent + permission
where_it_comes_from: Shared only if the customer logs in / consents via the platform.
what_it_means: The city/employer the person has self-declared on a profile, retrieved with their consent.
why_it_matters: A weak supporting hint at best — and only when truly consented; never a core source.
derived_columns: social_declared_city = the city the person lists on their own profile (only if they consented).

sits_in: Public web / social
where_it_comes_from: A public profile page link.
what_it_means: A public profile that might show a self-declared city or employer.
why_it_matters: Only a weak lead and high-risk for private individuals —
derived_columns: public_profile_city_hint = a city guessed from a public profile (weak — catalogue only).

sits_in: Social platforms
where_it_comes_from: Posts that carry a location tag.
what_it_means: Public posts with attached coordinates/place tags.
why_it_matters: Could reveal movement but crosses into surveillance of a private person??
derived_columns: (not used — catalogue only).

sits_in: Not actually much viable to source
where_it_comes_from: Circulates online after data breaches.
what_it_means: Stolen personal-data dumps of unknown accuracy.
why_it_matters: Acquire, process, validate, or prototype with breached data? (Different from the bank's own dormant-account flags, which are legitimate internal data.)
derived_columns: (not used — catalogue only).
